'''Athula Buddhagosha Attygalle''' ({{langx|si|අතුල ආටිගල}}) is a Sri Lankan scientist who works as a professor in the field of [[mass spectrometry]] in the United States. He was awarded the "Inventor of the Year" award in 2014 by the [[New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame]] for his work in mass spectrometric analysis utilizing helium plasma and charge-exchange [[ionization]] techniques. In 2017 Attygalle won an Edison Patent Award from the Research and Development Council of New Jersey for his patented work in mass spectrometric analysis utilizing helium-plasma and charge-exchange ionization techniques,<ref name="R&D Council Press Release">{{cite web | title=R&D Council Press Release | website=R&D Council Press Release | url=http://www.rdnj.org/news/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/RD-Council-Press-Release-TAEPA-Final-Nov-2.pdf | access-date=17 June 2018 | archive-date=18 June 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618002528/http://www.rdnj.org/news/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/RD-Council-Press-Release-TAEPA-Final-Nov-2.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> and the Arnold Berliner Award in 2021.<ref name="The Arnold Berliner Award 2021 honors research on bombardier beetles">{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s00114-021-01765-7 | title=The Arnold Berliner Award 2021 honors research on bombardier beetles | year=2021 | last1=Waltert | first1=Matthias | journal=The Science of Nature | volume=108 | issue=6 | page=53 | pmid=34636947 | pmc=8510909 | bibcode=2021SciNa.108...53W }}</ref>

==Education==
Attygalle had his primary and secondary education at [[Mahinda College]] in [[Galle]], [[Sri Lanka]].<ref name="mmss">{{cite book | title=Me Mahinda Shasthra Shala Hewath Madutu Mahindaya| publisher=Printhouse, Galle |year=2014|edition=2nd|page=239 }}</ref> After his school education, he entered the [[University of Peradeniya]] and obtained a BSc in chemistry in 1972. He then joined the [[University of Colombo]] and received a MSc in [[biochemistry]] in 1977. After obtaining a postgraduate diploma in chemistry and [[chemical engineering]] from the [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]], he obtained a PhD in chemistry from [[Keele University]] in 1983.<ref name="American Chemical Society">{{cite web | title=American Chemical Society | website=American Chemical Society | url=http://dgr.rints.com/faculty.cfm?id=S0064337 | access-date=24 July 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901112031/http://dgr.rints.com/faculty.cfm?id=S0064337 | archive-date=1 September 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==
After his doctorate, Attygalle was awarded a fellowship by the Humboldt Foundation to conduct research at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) under Hans Jürgen Bestmann, a pioneer in the field of insect pheromone synthesis.  Four years at FAU provided the impetus for Attygalle to become an expert in high-resolution mass spectrometry and micro-chemical techniques for structure elucidation of natural compounds at nanogram level.  At FAU, Attygalle championed in the area of lepidopteran sex pheromone identification. Attygalle was a visiting professor at [[University of Houston]], [[Texas]] and he has served as the director of the mass spectrometry facility at [[Cornell University]]. He has completed work there in GC-MS regarding insect substances and their identifications.<ref name="Gehrke Wixom Bayer 2001 p. 420">{{cite book | last1=Gehrke | first1=C.W. | last2=Wixom | first2=R.L. | last3=Bayer | first3=E. | title=Chromatography-A Century of Discovery 1900-2000.The Bridge to The Sciences/Technology | publisher=Elsevier Science | series=Journal of Chromatography Library | year=2001 | isbn=978-0-08-047650-6 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6jvNUq28_LEC&pg=PA420 | access-date=24 July 2017 | page=420}}</ref> Currently Attygalle is attached to the [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] as a research professor in the Department of Chemistry and head of the [[mass spectrometry]] laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://research.stevens.edu/athula-attygalle|title=Athula B. Attygalle {{!}} Nexus Research News {{!}} Stevens Institute of Technology {{!}} Schaefer School of Engineering and Science|website=research.stevens.edu|access-date=2017-07-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808115817/http://research.stevens.edu/athula-attygalle|archive-date=2017-08-08|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Attygalle was the recipient of the 2014 ‘Inventor of the Year’ award presented by the [[New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame]] for his patented work in Mass Spectrometric Analysis utilizing [[Helium]] Plasma and charge exchange ionization techniques.<ref name="Stevens Institute of Technology 2014">{{cite web | title=Professor Athula Attygalle Receives New Jersey 2014 Inventor of the Year Award | website=Stevens Institute of Technology | date=23 September 2014 | url=https://www.stevens.edu/news/professor-athula-attygalle-receives-new-jersey-2014-inventor-year-award | access-date=24 July 2017}}</ref>  Attygalle co-authored the 1999 article "Single-Site Catalysts for Ring-Opening Polymerization:  Synthesis of Heterotactic Poly(lactic acid) from rac-Lactide" in the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'', which has been widely cited.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Athula+B+Attygalle|title=Google Scholar search results for Athula B Attygalle|access-date=22 July 2017}}</ref>

In July 2025, Attygalle will receive an honorary degrees from [[Keele University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title=BAFTA winning actor and Olympic medal-winning siblings among Keele's summer honorary graduates |url=https://www.keele.ac.uk/about/news/2025/june/honorary-degree/summer-graduation-award.php |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=Keele University |language=en}}</ref>
